1. **US-1.AC-1** — WHEN [trigger] THE SYSTEM SHALL [behavior]
2. **US-1.AC-2** — WHILE [state], WHEN [trigger] THE SYSTEM SHALL [behavior]
3. **US-1.AC-3** — IF [error condition] THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL [recovery]
4. **US-1.AC-4** — [ubiquitous] THE SYSTEM SHALL [always-true property]

#### [SaaS] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
5. **US-1.AC-5** — WHEN a user from tenant A requests data, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT return any record whose tenant_id != A.
6. **US-1.AC-6** — THE SYSTEM SHALL respond within [N]ms at P95.

#### [AI] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
7. **US-1.AC-7** — THE SYSTEM SHALL produce outputs rated 'good or excellent' on at least [85]% of the golden eval set.
8. **US-1.AC-8** — IF the input contains a prompt-injection attempt, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL ignore the injected instruction and complete the original task.
9. **US-1.AC-9** — THE SYSTEM SHALL cost at most $[0.03] per user request at P95 size.

#### [SEC] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
10. **US-1.AC-10** — IF an unauthenticated request reaches a protected endpoint, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject it with 401 and return no protected data.
11. **US-1.AC-11** — IF an authenticated user requests a resource they are not authorized to access, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL deny it with 403 and record a security audit event.
12. **US-1.AC-12** — THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT include secrets, credentials, session tokens or stack traces in any response or log entry.

#### [PRIVACY] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
13. **US-1.AC-13** — WHEN a data subject requests a copy of their personal data, THE SYSTEM SHALL export it in a structured, machine-readable format within one month.
14. **US-1.AC-14** — WHEN a data subject's erasure request is accepted, THE SYSTEM SHALL delete or irreversibly anonymize their personal data in every store within one month.
15. **US-1.AC-15** — WHEN a record's retention period ends, THE SYSTEM SHALL delete or anonymize it.

#### [DIST] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
16. **US-1.AC-16** — IF publishing [the event] fails after the database transaction commits, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL still deliver it later, at least once, without losing it (transactional outbox).
17. **US-1.AC-17** — WHEN the same message is delivered more than once, THE SYSTEM SHALL apply its effect exactly once (idempotent consumer).
18. **US-1.AC-18** — WHEN two requests update the same [entity] concurrently, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT lose either update (optimistic locking or a unique constraint).
19. **US-1.AC-19** — IF [the dependency] is unavailable, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL [degrade / retry with exponential backoff and jitter] and SHALL NOT block [the critical path].

#### [API] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
20. **US-1.AC-20** — IF a request omits [a required field] or sends it malformed, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 400 with an application/problem+json body that names the field and carries a stable error code.
21. **US-1.AC-21** — WHEN a client repeats [a create request] with the same Idempotency-Key and body, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the first response without applying the effect again.
22. **US-1.AC-22** — IF an update carries an If-Match ETag that no longer matches the resource, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 412 and leave the resource unchanged.
23. **US-1.AC-23** — IF a change to the contract would break an existing client, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL ship it only in a new [API version] and keep the current version working until its announced Sunset date.

#### [UI] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
24. **US-1.AC-24** — WHEN a user operates [the view] with the keyboard alone, THE SYSTEM SHALL make every action reachable and operable in a logical focus order, with a visible focus indicator.
25. **US-1.AC-25** — IF a submitted form has invalid fields, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL keep every value the user entered, identify each error in text next to its field and move focus to an error summary.
26. **US-1.AC-26** — WHILE [the list] has no items, THE SYSTEM SHALL show an empty state that explains why and offers the next action.
27. **US-1.AC-27** — IF loading [the data] fails, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL show an error message with a Retry action and keep the content already shown.

#### [OBS] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
28. **US-1.AC-28** — THE SYSTEM SHALL emit [the request metric] with its latency, outcome and a correlation ID for every [request], and log each error with that correlation ID and no personal data.
29. **US-1.AC-29** — WHEN the error-budget burn rate of [the SLO] exceeds [14.4]× over [one hour], THE SYSTEM SHALL page the on-call engineer with a link to the runbook.
30. **US-1.AC-30** — IF the canary's error rate exceeds [the baseline] by [N] percentage points, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL stop the rollout and roll back to the previous version automatically.
31. **US-1.AC-31** — WHILE [a dependency] is unavailable, THE SYSTEM SHALL report itself not ready (readiness check) while staying live, and recover without a restart once it is back.

#### [DATA] Acceptance Criteria (EARS)
32. **US-1.AC-32** — WHEN a batch contains a row that violates [a data-quality rule], THE SYSTEM SHALL quarantine that row with the rule it failed and SHALL NOT load it into [the target table].
33. **US-1.AC-33** — IF the job is re-run for a partition that was already loaded, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL produce the same result as a single run, with no duplicate and no missing rows (an idempotent re-run and backfill).
34. **US-1.AC-34** — IF the newest data in [the table] is older than [its freshness SLA], THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL alert [the owner] and mark the table stale for its consumers.
35. **US-1.AC-35** — WHEN the schema of [the source] changes, THE SYSTEM SHALL accept an additive, backward-compatible change and SHALL reject a breaking change (a removed or renamed column, a narrowed type) before any row reaches [the consumers].
